data.narrative:
Tempo is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Nima Rahmatian, Kelvin Randhir, Joerg Petrasch, and Alessandro Bo. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine private climate and energy companies—including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—plus one public comparable (LNZA). Tempo has raised $50M to date.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised of $50M as a baseline proxy and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the next funding stage yields an implied valuation of $100M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy cohort meeting minimum thresholds for statistical confidence.

The triangulated valuation range is $85M to $115M, with a median of $100M. This range reflects the stage-progression methodology applied with conservative and elevated scenarios. Key uncertainties center on the lack of granular peer multiples at Tempo's specific stage and the heterogeneous nature of the climate tech sector, where comparable companies span diverse technology types and commercialization timelines. Any refined valuation would benefit from tighter peer filtering or observed pricing from recent comparable Series A transactions in the sector.
